key_insight: Co-PiLOT turns inverse design into constrained optimization in a learned latent space, using a generative decoder as a validity prior and a physics-informed optimizer to search for target microstructures.
engineering_relevance: For magnesium alloy design, it offers a practical path to faster microstructure/texture optimization while respecting manufacturability and crystal-plasticity simulation constraints.
method: ViT encoder compresses EBSD-derived microstructures into a low-dimensional latent code.
Latent decoders (latent diffusion, DiT, rectified-flow) reconstruct candidate microstructures with a learned feasibility prior.
MERIDIAN optimizes the latent variables with uncertainty-aware, feasibility-aware, and manifold-aware acquisition under a simulation budget.
evidence_signal: On ~80,000 EBSD-derived samples, the ViT-FMDiT model achieved FID 27.86 and MS-SSIM 0.178, and paired with MERIDIAN reduced relative target error by 3%–22% versus seven baselines within 160 simulations.
watch_item: Performance depends on decoder fidelity and the quality of feasibility predictions, so errors in reconstruction or solver coupling could mislead the optimizer.
paper_title: Co-PiLOT: Constrained Physics-Informed Latent Optimization for Target-Driven Inverse Design
